buffer(3) Library Functions Manual buffer(3)

NAME

buffer - Owned Buffers


- Bounded aligned storage, explicit ownership and worker workspaces.

SYNOPSIS

Detailed Description

Bounded aligned storage, explicit ownership and worker workspaces.

Owned Buffers

Payload pointers returned by buffer_alloc() are ownership tokens. Their capacity, logical length, alignment and owning domain are stored privately. buffer_release(pointer) releases one reference and clears the typed pointer. Only the owning pointer may be queried or released: interior pointers and views into stack, codec or external storage remain borrowed.

Ownership

void *payload = buffer_alloc(NULL, 4096);
if (!payload)


  return SET_ERRNO(ERROR_MEMORY, "Payload budget exhausted");
// Fill payload before publication.
asciichat_error_t result = packet_queue_push_take(queue, PACKET_TYPE_PING,


                                                 &payload, 4096, 0);
// Success clears payload. Failure leaves it here for retry or release.
buffer_release(payload);

buffer_share() creates an additional immutable reference. Every recipient releases its own reference. Mutation, including changing logical length, requires exclusive ownership. Reference counting does not synchronize access to payload contents. A transport retains ownership until its actual completion contract permits release; caching memory does not extend a borrowed lifetime.

Domains and limits

buffer_domain_create() supplies an isolated capacity-class cache and budget. A mutex serializes allocation, return and trimming. There is no concurrent free-list reclamation, ABA-sensitive stack, or allocator-origin guessing. Backing allocations use the existing tracked allocation machinery. Manually aligning within that allocation means Windows uses the matching ordinary deallocator, without mixing aligned_malloc and free.

Domain limits include backing capacity, payload headers and alignment padding. Defaults allow 512 MiB process-wide, reserving 8 MiB for control traffic. The default media domain allows 504 MiB with at most 32 MiB cached. Queue domains allow 64 MiB with at most 8 MiB cached, in addition to queue byte limits. These are bounded storage budgets, not a guarantee that every request succeeds. The process budget also accounts for domain objects, including closed domains retained by outstanding buffers. Oversized blocks are budgeted but not cached. Exhaustion returns ERROR_MEMORY; no heap fallback bypasses the limit. Control traffic has a bounded reserved allowance through buffer_control_domain(). This budget covers this API's storage, not the entire process RSS or third-party codec allocations. Platform mappings hold buffer_budget_t leases against the same process cap; they are unmapped instead of recycled after zero-copy cancellation. Kernel-pinned pages may outlive a discarded mapping until the kernel releases them. Cache trim returns allocations to the backing allocator; it does not promise that the OS immediately reduces RSS.

buffer_domain_close() stops admissions and frees cached storage. Join users of the domain pointer first. Outstanding payloads keep the domain alive and may be released afterwards, including by another thread. The last release reclaims a closed domain. Application startup/shutdown owns the default domains.

Repeated work

Zero-initialize buffer_workspace_t. buffer_workspace_reserve() retains capacity across frames and preserves existing storage on failure. Destroy the workspace when its worker stops. Compression workspaces retain the zstd context too. Frame-send workspaces retain compression storage; vectored sends borrow slices. Render file contexts retain pixel-copy storage. Audio prepares storage when streams or mixer membership change, outside the sample mixing loop.

Validation

Build test-buffer-ownership and run ctest -R '^buffer-ownership$'. This native suite runs on Windows, Linux and macOS without Criterion. It tests alignment, size-class reuse, overflow, exhaustion, immutable sharing, failure preservation, shutdown with outstanding owners, concurrent trimming, MPMC ownership transfer, process-wide exhaustion with control reserve, queues and media storage. ASan builds poison cached payloads to expose access after the final release.
